name: Mesoridazine
summary: Mesoridazine is an older antipsychotic once used for schizophrenia; it was withdrawn from the US market in 2004 because of the risk of dangerous heart-rhythm changes.
description: Mesoridazine is an older (phenothiazine) antipsychotic that was used to treat schizophrenia. It is made in the body from thioridazine and works mainly by blocking dopamine D2 receptors, which eases symptoms like hallucinations and delusions. It was withdrawn from the U.S. market in 2004 because it can cause a heart-rhythm change that can be dangerous (QT prolongation), including torsades de pointes (a life-threatening heart rhythm).

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Mesoridazine is a piperidine phenothiazine antipsychotic indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia. It is a metabolite of thioridazine and works primarily by antagonizing dopamine D2 receptors, reducing positive symptoms of psychosis. It was withdrawn from the U.S. market in 2004 due to risk of QT prolongation and serious ventricular arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes.
